title: Language Models and Society
tagline: Bias, privacy, copyright, misinformation, work, energy and governance
summary: Language models are changing how people learn, work and communicate. This course examines bias and fairness, privacy and memorisation, copyright and data provenance, misinformation and persuasion, effects on work and education, the energy and environmental cost of models, open and closed release, and how laws and institutions are responding.

chapters.title: Bias and fairness
chapters.summary: Sources of bias in data and models, and how it is measured and mitigated.

chapters.title: Privacy and memorisation
chapters.summary: Extraction of training data, personal data and privacy-preserving techniques.

chapters.title: Copyright and data provenance
chapters.summary: Training on copyrighted works, licences, opt-outs and attribution.

chapters.title: Misinformation and persuasion
chapters.summary: Synthetic text at scale, persuasion, watermarking and detection.

chapters.title: Work, education and the economy
chapters.summary: Productivity, effects on the labour market, and learning with AI.

chapters.title: Energy and the environment
chapters.summary: Energy use and emissions of training and inference, and trends in efficiency.

chapters.title: Open and closed models
chapters.summary: Open weights and closed APIs, licences, and the trade-offs of each.

chapters.title: Governance and regulation
chapters.summary: AI laws, standards and international coordination.
